reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises: it confirms the feasibility of the coating system on C45 steel, specifies the 25–35% bonding mass range for improved adhesion and hardness, describes the resulting microstructure, and reports the microhardness range (HV 8.5–15, which corresponds to ~8.5–15 GPa). However, the hypothesis overstates the quantitative wear improvement (up to 5 times lower) and the specific microhardness target (approaching 15.0 GPa vs. baseline 8.5 GPa) as these exact comparative values are not provided in the cited passages.
premises: ESD with Co-Ni-Cr-B-Si bonding mass and WC, B4C, TiB2 superhard particles can produce composite coatings on C45 steel
A bonding mass content of 25–35% yields coatings with improved adhesion, higher hardness, and toughness
Optimal pulse energy provides dense, uniform coatings with crystalline-amorphous structures and wear-resistant phases
Coating microhardness can reach up to 15 GPa (HV 8.5–15 range)
Coatings exhibit improved wear resistance compared to untreated substrate
